articles.title: What I got wrong estimating LLM costs before the request
articles.excerpt: Ever since AI has taken over the internet, I've been wondering how we can optimize the full ability of AI in our life. Therefore I began building a small gateway that sits between your code and the Op…
articles.body: Ever since AI has taken over the internet, I've been wondering how we can optimize the full ability of AI in our life. Therefore I began building a small gateway that sits between your code and the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini APIs. It has one job: if a request would push today's spend past a daily cap you set, refuse it before it goes out. Why bother? Because the stories are always the same. An agent gets stuck in a loop, keeps retrying, every retry sends a longer conversation, and nobody notices until the bill shows up. Logs and alerts tell you what happened. I wanted something that says no before it happens. (To be fair to OpenAI: they now have hard spend limits , and you should turn them on.

articles.title: Building a Production REST API in Rust with Express-Like Simplicity
articles.excerpt: Building a Production REST API in Rust with Express-Like Simplicity If you come from the JavaScript (Express/Fastify) or Python (FastAPI/Flask) worlds, you are used to building APIs at the speed of th…
articles.body: Building a Production REST API in Rust with Express-Like Simplicity If you come from the JavaScript (Express/Fastify) or Python (FastAPI/Flask) worlds, you are used to building APIs at the speed of thought. You define a route, parse JSON from the body, extract URL parameters, and return a response. When web developers transition to traditional Rust web frameworks like Axum or Actix, they often hit a brick wall. Routing requires managing complex extractor tuples ( Path , Query , Json , State ), and one misplaced generic type triggers compiler errors that look like cryptographic puzzles. In this guide, we will build a complete, production-ready CRUD REST API in Rust in under 15 minutes using Nitrox —without fighting trait bounds or lifetime errors.

articles.title: When the mesh fights Kubernetes: a webhook deadlock, a probe loop, and what it costs
articles.excerpt: In part 1, we rigged the network so every packet in the pod passes through Ananse's sidecar, without the app knowing. That was the plan on paper. This post is about what happened when the plan met a r…
articles.body: In part 1 , we rigged the network so every packet in the pod passes through Ananse's sidecar, without the app knowing. That was the plan on paper. This post is about what happened when the plan met a real cluster. Two bugs taught me the most. In the first, the mesh locked its own control plane out of the cluster. In the second, a routine health check made the sidecar call itself until it drowned in timeouts. After that, I'll cover what running the mesh actually costs, and what I'd change next. The Deadlock (The Webhook Injecting Into Its Own Namespace) In Ananse Service Mesh, the control plane runs a Mutating Admission Webhook. Crucially, this webhook is configured with failurePolicy: Fail . This is a deliberate security choice: if the webhook cannot be reached, pod creation is rejected.

articles.body: Most health apps treat consent as a checkbox at signup. Patients tick "I agree", and from then on every integration, every clinician and every AI assistant reads everything, forever. That model breaks the moment a patient asks a reasonable question: "Can my cardiologist see my lab results for the next month, but not my mental-health notes?" FHIR R4 already has the building block for this: the Consent resource. Here is how we model scoped, time-limited, revocable consent with it, and the enforcement traps we hit along the way.

articles.title: Your CRM Import Needs a Dry Run: How to Stop Duplicates Before They Happen
articles.excerpt: Most CRM data problems are not caused by bad data. They are caused by a bad match key and an import that wrote straight to production. This post describes one pattern that prevents most of it: plan fi…
articles.body: Most CRM data problems are not caused by bad data. They are caused by a bad match key and an import that wrote straight to production. This post describes one pattern that prevents most of it: plan first, write second. The import script produces a plan of what it would do, a human checks the counts, and only then does it write. It works with HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, or a Postgres table. The concepts are the same. The problem You have a CSV of 500 leads from an enrichment tool. You push it into the CRM. A week later someone notices three records for the same person and two companies called "Acme" with different domains. What went wrong was upstream of the CRM. The import never decided what "the same person" means.

articles.excerpt: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft has gotten its first close-up look at the Didymos binary asteroid, the first space rock system "punched" by humanity.
articles.body: The Didymos binary asteroid system, as seen by Europe's Hera probe. The main asteroid, Didymos, dominates the frame while just a sliver of its "moonlet," Dimorphos, is visible beneath it. ESA released this image on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: ESA) The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Hera spacecraft has gotten its first close-up look at the Didymos binary asteroid system. If that system sounds familiar, it's because it made headlines in September 2022 when NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) spacecraft smashed into it. The aim of the DART mission was to test whether an impact could divert an asteroid away from a collision course with Earth. The purpose of Hera is to follow up on DART by making up-close observations of the Didymos system.

articles.body: The northern lights could put on an impressive display this weekend as a colossal coronal hole on the sun fires a stream of high-speed solar wind toward Earth. Minor (G1) geomagnetic storm conditions between Nov. 6 and Nov. 8, with a chance of moderate (G2) conditions on Nov. 7 and Nov. 8, according to NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) . If G2 conditions materialize, the northern lights could be visible as far south as New York and Idaho. What is happening? The culprit behind the potential uptick in northern lights is a large coronal hole on the sun , a region where the sun's magnetic field opens up. They allow streams of charged particles known as the solar wind to escape more easily into space.

articles.title: 4-billion-year-old 'Rosetta Stone' found in Sahara Desert could unlock the secret history of water on Mars
articles.excerpt: A rock discovered in the Sahara Desert formed more than 4.1 billion years ago, making it one of the oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The ancient space rock offers a rare glimpse into the formatio…
articles.body: A rose-colored rock discovered in the Sahara Desert may hold some clues to Mars' ancient geological history. The meteorite , named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered in 2022, weighs roughly 1.8 pounds (800 grams) and formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Blasted off Mars by an impact before eventually landing on Earth, it is one of the three oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The extraordinary age and unusual mineral composition of Teghaza 001 offer a rare glimpse into the formation of Mars' early crust and how volcanic materials may have been altered by water, according to a statement from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California.
